mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (GDPC1) create a dual slowdown in economic activity that depresses investor confidence and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while GDPC1 decreases by >3% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening coupled with demand weakness
failure_condition: A Granger causality test shows PAYEMS changes do not precede GDPC1 changes at the 5% significance level, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies move in opposite directions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% month-over-month signals pent-up consumer demand that anticipates future earnings growth, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of >2% MoM HOUST growth, the 5-day forward returns show no positive correlation with the sales surge (Pearson's rho < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index) for two consecutive months indicates supply-side constraints that raise uncertainty and lower S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of INDPRO contraction, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that spurs monetary policy easing, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE crosses below 3.5% but FEDFUNDS remains unchanged, 60-day forward returns show no positive effect (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in labor force participation (PAYEMS) combined with a decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests demographic expansion without cost pressures, which supports optimism and drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while CPIAUCSL decreases by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction between PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL is not statistically significant in explaining 20-day returns (F-statistic < 1).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a post-pandemic recovery characterized by rising consumer confidence (measured indirectly via a composite of S&P 500 options skew) and sustained GDP momentum (not directly observable here) predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns regardless of other proxies.
failure_condition: Over 12 months in the 'post-pandemic recovery' regime, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months, without a corresponding change in the federal funds rate, create expectations of future rate cuts that boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of CPIAUCSL < 2% for >4 months and FEDFUNDS unchanged, 20-day forward returns show no positive trend (slope < 0 in rolling regression).
